stories.title: Is this how the world ends? Extinction scenarios are taking over the AI debate.
stories.simple_summary: People are increasingly worried that artificial intelligence could lead to dangerous or even catastrophic scenarios. These worries are now a major part of conversations about AI's future.
stories.why_it_matters: This mostly matters to policymakers and researchers — you should be aware that safety concerns exist, but there's no action you need to take today.

stories.title: World leaders meet at UN as planet grapples with war, runaway AI and climate shocks
stories.simple_summary: World leaders are meeting to discuss major global problems, including concerns about AI, war, and climate change.
stories.why_it_matters: This is about government discussions; nothing specific you need to do right now.

stories.title: Lawmakers push for artificial intelligence regulations
stories.simple_summary: Government officials are trying to create rules for how AI companies should operate.
stories.why_it_matters: This could eventually affect what AI tools you can use and how they work, but it's still in the early discussion stage.

stories.title: AI programs can interfere with key lessons of childhood. Here’s what parents can do
stories.simple_summary: AI programs can sometimes interfere with what children normally learn from everyday experience. The article offers advice for parents.
stories.why_it_matters: If you have grandchildren, you might want to read this to understand how screens with AI differ from older technology.

stories.title: U.S. and China Discuss System to Warn of A.I. National Security Issues
stories.simple_summary: The United States and China are talking about creating a system to alert each other if AI causes national security problems.
stories.why_it_matters: This is mostly about government and military concerns — nothing that affects your daily life or business.

stories.title: Amazon doesn’t trust Meta’s Muse AI agent
stories.simple_summary: Amazon blocked Meta's AI helper from shopping on Amazon.com on behalf of users because Meta didn't ask permission first.
stories.why_it_matters: If you use Amazon or Meta services, good news: companies are setting boundaries to protect customers from unauthorized AI actions.

stories.title: Nvidia boss says there is ‘0% chance’ AI destroys the world by 2030 | AI (artificial intelligence)
stories.simple_summary: The boss of Nvidia (a big computer chip company) said he's certain AI won't destroy the world by 2030.
stories.why_it_matters: This is mostly one person's opinion; it's worth noting that people disagree on AI safety risks, but this headline alone doesn't change anything for you.

stories.title: 6 days left to save up to $200 to TechCrunch Disrupt 2026
stories.simple_summary: A tech conference is advertising discounted tickets for the next six days.
stories.why_it_matters: This is just a sales announcement — nothing you need to act on unless you want to attend a tech conference.

stories.title: First Came Space Force. Now Prepare For AI Force
stories.simple_summary: The government might create an official military or defense branch focused specifically on artificial intelligence.
stories.why_it_matters: This is mostly relevant to government and military policy — it doesn't directly affect small businesses or ordinary people.

stories.title: World model companies are keeping a lot of secrets
stories.simple_summary: Companies building advanced AI 'world models' (computer programs that learn to understand how the real world works) are not sharing details about what they're making.
stories.why_it_matters: This mostly matters to investors and tech professionals — nothing you need to know for your own use of AI.

stories.title: Is the AI industry really ready to slow down?
stories.simple_summary: Tech industry leaders are debating whether they're actually willing to slow down AI development.
stories.why_it_matters: This is industry gossip; whether companies slow down or speed up doesn't immediately affect you, though it could matter long-term.

stories.title: No one is surprised that Nvidia’s Jensen Huang thinks AI fears are overblown
stories.simple_summary: The leader of Nvidia (which makes computer chips used for AI) dismissed safety worries about AI, saying the fears are exaggerated.
stories.why_it_matters: It's worth knowing that the people making money from AI might downplay risks — but this is one person's opinion, not a fact you need to act on.
